At approximately 14:30 SGT, patient experienced sudden onset of severe epigastric pain radiating to back, associated with nausea and two episodes of vomiting. Patient self-administered paracetamol 1 g without relief. At 17:45 SGT, patient was brought to Raffles Hospital Emergency Department by family member.

On arrival, patient was in visible distress. Vital signs: BP 148/92 mmHg, HR 112 bpm, RR 20/min, Temp 37.8°C, SpO2 97% on room air. Abdominal exam revealed epigastric tenderness with guarding, no rebound. Bowel sounds present but reduced.

- Serum amylase: 890 U/L (ref: 28–100)

Patient was admitted to medical ward at 23:00 SGT. Management initiated: IV fluids (lactated Ringer's), IV pantoprazole, IV ondansetron, nil by mouth initially. Morphine PCA for pain control.

**SECTION C: SERIOUS ADVERSE EVENT DESCRIPTION**

**Diagnosis / Event Term (MedDRA v26.0):** Acute pancreatitis

**Date of Onset:** 2026-06-11, approximately 14:30 SGT
**Date of Diagnosis:** 2026-06-11, 19:10 SGT (emergency department)

**Narrative:**

Patient received first dose of study drug at 08:05 SGT on 2026-06-11. At approximately 14:30 SGT, patient experienced sudden onset of severe epigastric pain radiating to back, associated with nausea and two episodes of vomiting. Patient self-administered paracetamol 1 g without relief. At 17:45 SGT, patient was brought to Raffles Hospital Emergency Department by family member.

On arrival, patient was in visible distress. Vital signs: BP 148/92 mmHg, HR 112 bpm, RR 20/min, Temp 37.8°C, SpO2 97% on room air. Abdominal exam revealed epigastric tenderness with guarding, no rebound. Bowel sounds present but reduced.

Laboratory results (19:10 SGT):
- Serum lipase: 1,240 U/L (ref: 13–60)
- Serum amylase: 890 U/L (ref: 28–100)
- ALT: 45 U/L, AST: 38 U/L, ALP: 92 U/L, Total bilirubin: 12 µmol/L
- Triglycerides: 1.8 mmol/L
- Calcium: 2.31 mmol/L
- WBC: 14.2 × 10⁹/L, Hb 13.1 g/dL, Platelets 245 × 10⁹/L
- CRP: 48 mg/L

Abdominal ultrasound (20:15 SGT): Gallbladder normal, no gallstones, no biliary duct dilation. Pancreas not well visualized due to bowel gas.

CT abdomen with contrast (21:30 SGT): Diffuse enlargement of pancreas with peripancreatic fat stranding, consistent with acute interstitial pancreatitis. No necrosis, no fluid collections, no pseudocyst.

Patient was admitted to medical ward at 23:00 SGT. Management initiated: IV fluids (lactated Ringer's), IV pantoprazole, IV ondansetron, nil by mouth initially. Morphine PCA for pain control.

**Causality Assessment (Investigator):** Possibly related. No alternative etiology identified; patient has no history of gallstones, alcohol use, or prior pancreatitis. Onset occurred within 6 hours of first dose of study drug. Temporal relationship is suggestive.

**Seriousness Criteria:** Hospitalization (initial or prolonged) – patient admitted for inpatient care.
